regime.summary: Policy rate held at 10.5% but the 6M bill sits 1.00pp above it, so the market prices hikes. CPI is rising and Brent is up 81% in three months. KSE100 fell 14.6% in a month with heavy foreign selling. The rupee is steady. This resembles a tightening-plus-oil shock, not a clean 2025-style event, so I hold the core at reduced size and keep cash.

evidence.quote: Policy rate 10.5%; last MPC decision 2026-03-09: hold (+0bp)
Regime: 6M T-bill minus policy rate +1.00pp (market pricing hikes); CPI rising over 3 months (+0.8pp)
Tightening plus external stress: rate up 800bp in ten months with CPI above it. To June 2023 the median liquid stock fell 52% and 4 of 95 names rose.
Lesson: hold the core; keep cash ready for a weekend gap.

core.thesis: E&P is the one direct Brent link; Brent is up 81% in three months. MARI is the E&P name whose latest quarter EPS rose year on year, so it is growing, not merely stable. Drawdown of 20% from high is inside what the investor accepts. Business quality (sponsor, reinvestment) is not in the bundle.

evidence.quote: A8. Oil: where is Brent, and which link do I actually hold?

core.thesis: Latest quarter EPS up strongly year on year on a low P/E, with seven results filings in the pack. Power is one of three sectors still positive over 6 months. Not oil-linked, so it diversifies the E&P holding. The yield is high, but the aim here is the earnings recovery, not income.

evidence.quote: B13. Is it growing, not merely stable?

core.thesis: Holding-company name that has held up: positive over 3 and 6 months while the market and most sectors fell. Fertilizer is a sector with positive 6-month return. A material-information filing on 2026-03-13 is unexplained in the pack. Latest quarter EPS fell, so this is a smaller position.

watch.subject: Next SBP MPC decision
watch.trigger: If the SBP hikes and the 6M bill does not rise further, treat the hike as priced and deploy part of the cash into the core names. If it holds while the bill stays above the policy rate, keep the cash.

watch.subject: KSE100 after a 14.6% one-month fall
watch.trigger: A first up session after a visible low, with foreign corporate selling slowing from the 20-session pace, would justify adding to the core. The base rate for buying a bare index shock is unproven, so a known trigger is required.

evidence.quote: no word given (Verdict 3: buy only on a known trigger)

watch.subject: CRTM
watch.trigger: Do not buy. Eight upper locks in 10 days and a 192% one-month gain; the measured result for this type is nothing, with a median loss. Revisit only if a filing explains the move.

exposure_reason: Default is the core at about 75%. I hold 55%: the bill is 1.00pp over the policy rate (hikes priced), CPI is rising and Brent is up 81%, which matches the tightening-plus-external-stress analogue where the median stock fell 52%. Against that, the 2025 shock lesson says hold the core, and no tested timing signal exists in either direction. So the core stays on business grounds, tilted to Brent and positive-6m sectors, with 45% cash for a priced-in hike or a known trigger. Cement, autos and steel are excluded.
not_known: Reserves, current account and IMF status (market.md says not available). Sponsor quality, reinvestment returns and balance sheets of the core names. Whether the Brent move is a run or a spike. The next MPC date and what the market expects.
contamination_note: I have some general recollection of how Pakistan's market evolved after this date from training. I did not use it and chose the exposure and names from the bundle alone. If any of it leaked into the choice of Brent-linked and positive-6m sectors, it is not cited here; every citation is a bundle string.
